title: ML-Assisted Triage and Runbook Automation Roadmap
author: Claire Nguyen
content:
Summary
-------
This roadmap describes Redwood's plan to introduce ML-assisted operator tooling for triage and runbook automation across the platform-operator surface. The initiative focuses on reducing mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolution (MTTR) for multi-tenant inference degradations by 30% within 12 months while keeping operator cognitive load and false-positive automation under strict guardrails.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- MTTA reduction: target 25% within 6 months, 40% within 12 months for P1/P2 incidents where automation applies.
- MTTR reduction: target 30% within 12 months for incidents with deterministic remediation paths.
- Operator acceptability: >= 85% operator approval for recommended actions in pilot cohort.
- Safety: <= 2% accidental automated rollbacks that require operator revert in pilot group.
- Coverage: ML-assist should meaningfully surface recommendations for at least 50% of high-frequency incident classes (prefix-cache misses, token-burst forensics, GPU preemption spikes).

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Platform operators spend a disproportionate amount of time on repetitive triage tasks: classifying signal combs, matching incidents to known runbooks, filling initial incident context, and executing routine remediation steps (cache drains, model swaps, transient throttles). A combination of structured telemetry, labeled historical incidents, and canonical runbook actions creates an opportunity to apply lightweight ML ranking + deterministic automation to reduce operator work and improve consistency.

Scope
-----
Included:
- Triage recommendation model (incident-class ranker) that maps telemetry bundles to the most-likely runbook(s).
- Action suggestion layer (human-in-the-loop) that proposes a ranked list of operator actions with confidence scores.
- Safe automation hooks for fully automated tasks with explicit guardrails (e.g., prefetched cache refresh, model variant swap to a pinned-compatible quantized variant) behind opt-in policies.
- Dashboards & alerting changes to surface recommendations and model health.

Excluded:
- Autonomous state changes for customer-visible tenant throttles without explicit tenant-owner approval.
- Cross-region failovers as first-phase automated actions.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
Services involved (examples):
- incident-scorer: a microservice that consumes consolidated telemetry bundles from telemetry-fanout and returns ranked runbooks and action items.
- runbook-store: canonical JSON/YAML runbook repository (already exists) with stable IDs and action primitives.
- operator-assist-ui: Console surface that shows ranked recommendations in the incident panel, allows one-click action execution for approved primitives.
- automation-gateway: performs guarded automation calls with audit logging and reversible checkpoints.
- ml-metrics-exporter: exports training and inference metrics to prometheus/telemetry-fanout and feeds the model-eval pipeline.

Data and model requirements
---------------------------
- Training data: 24 months of labeled incidents, labeled by incident class and remediations (anonymized). Minimum dataset size: 8k incidents across major classes.
- Features: token-latency histograms, KV-prefix-hit ratios, GPU preemption counters, tenant-priority, call-graph fingerprints, recent rollout history.
- Model constraints: concise ranker (<20ms P95 inference), explainability hooks (top contributing signals), and versioned model artifacts stored in model-registry.

SLOs and operational constraints
--------------------------------
- incident-scorer P95 latency <= 25ms for operator UI RPCs.
- automation-gateway audit log retention: 1 year (indexed by runbook ID and tenant).
- Model rollback safety: automatic rollback if recommendation precision on live traffic drops > 10% vs baseline within 24h.
- Canary policy: start with read-only recommendations for first 6 weeks per region; enable human-in-loop action execution in pilot after operator signoff.

Milestones and timeline
-----------------------
Quarter-by-quarter plan (high level):
- Q1 2026: Discovery & data hygiene
  1) Inventory runbook-store and tag canonical remediations with primitives.
  2) Curate and anonymize incident dataset; define label schema and labeling SOP.
  3) Prototype incident-scorer: baseline TF-IDF + gradient-boosted ranker on vectorized telemetry.
- Q2 2026: MVP & pilot
  1) Deploy incident-scorer in read-only mode hooked into the incident console.
  2) Instrument ml-metrics-exporter and set up model-eval dashboards (precision/recall, operator override rate).
  3) Run 2-week pilot with platform-operator cohort A in us-west-2 region.
- Q3 2026: Human-in-loop execution and limited automation
  1) Launch operator-assist-ui one-click action flow for approved primitives.
  2) Implement automation-gateway with reversible checkpoints and dry-run audit trails.
  3) Measure operator acceptance and false-positive rate; freeze automation primitives list.
- Q4 2026: Broader rollout and SRE integration
  1) Expand pilot to additional regions (eu-central-1) and platform teams.
  2) Integrate model health alerts into platform SLO dashboards; define automatic rollback triggers.
  3) Document runbook changes and authoring guidelines for ML-readability.
- Q1 2027: Optimization and road to scale
  1) Iterate model to incorporate embeddings and lightweight sequence features for higher recall.
  2) Begin safe full-automation experiments for low-blast-radius primitives (non-customer-visible cache refreshes).
  3) Cost/benefit analysis and decision to move to org-wide rollout or refocus.

Implementation playbook (operator-facing)
----------------------------------------
1) Pilot opt-in: Operators must opt-in per region via the Console > Settings > Operator Labs.
2) Review recommendations: For each active incident, incident-scorer will display 3 recommended runbook IDs with confidence and top-3 contributing signals.
3) Execute with confirmation: One-click actions require a confirmation modal for primitives with irreversible effects.
4) Feedback loop: Operators can mark recommendations as useful/not useful; these labels feed the nightly training job.

Example operator CLI (for scripted runbook execution)
-----------------------------------------------------
# fetch recommendations for incident 2026-IL-42
redwoodctl incidents recommend --incident-id 2026-IL-42 --region us-west-2

# execute recommended action (human has confirmed it)
redwoodctl runbook execute --runbook-id rb-prefetch-refresh-v2 --incident 2026-IL-42 --dry-run=false

Example runbook-store JSON primitive (simplified)
--------------------------------------------------
{
  "runbook_id": "rb-prefetch-refresh-v2",
  "title": "KV prefix prefetch refresh",
  "primitives": ["prefetch_refresh", "verify_kv_hit_increase"],
  "blast_radius": "low",
  "required_approvals": ["operator"],
  "rollback": "prefetch-recover-state"
}

Monitoring and dashboards
-------------------------
- New dashboards:
  - ML Assist: recommendation precision/recall by incident class (per-region)
  - Operator UX: recommendation acceptance rate, median decision latency
  - Automation Safety: audit log volume, automated-action revert rate
- Alerting changes:
  - Create a paged alert (P3) when recommendation precision falls below 60% for 6 consecutive hours in a region.
  - Auto-create a ticket in triage-board when automation-gateway fails > 0.1% of attempts in 1h window.

Data governance and privacy
---------------------------
- Anonymization: no tenant-identifying fields should be present in model training payloads; use tenant-hash with reversible mapping stored in a KMS-protected vault for post-hoc investigation.
- Access controls: model-registry, runbook-store, and automation-gateway require RBAC role: platform-operator, platform-sre, platform-admin.
- Audit trail: all suggested actions and executed automations must be immutable-log entries with executor identity, timestamp, and playback hook.

Experimentation & evaluation
----------------------------
- A/B plan: split incoming incidents into control vs. ML-assist buckets (10/90 for early experiments) by region and tenant cohort.
- Evaluation metrics: precision@1, recall@3 for recommended runbooks, operator override rate, MTTR delta, cost of incorrect automations.
- Nightly retrain: schedule nightly incremental training job that incorporates new operator feedback for the prior 48h window. Full retrain weekly.

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: automation misfires cause customer-visible regressions.
  Mitigation: start with low-blast-radius primitives and implement automatic safety rollback checkpoints and circuit-breaker on a per-primitive basis.
- Risk: model drift on new modes of failure (e.g., novel model variants or hardware changes).
  Mitigation: model-eval monitors and auto-disable on precision drop; maintain a fallback deterministic rule-engine.
- Risk: operator mistrust and low adoption.
  Mitigation: invest in explainability UI, provide manual feedback paths, and mandate read-only mode for first 6 weeks.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Product lead: Claire Nguyen (eng-platform) — roadmap, KPIs, and operator engagement.
- ML lead: Samir Rao (applied-ml-and-evals) — model design, training pipeline, evaluation.
- Infra/Runtime: Jordan Lee (eng-serving-runtime) — latency & runtime constraints, automation gateways.
- Operator liaison: Priya Malhotra (eng-sre) — pilot coordination and operator training.

Acceptance criteria for GA
-------------------------
- Recommendation precision@1 >= 70% across pilot classes and regions.
- Operator acceptance rate >= 50% (meaningful adoption) for non-trivial recommendations.
- No high-severity customer impact incidents caused by automated actions during the 90-day expanded pilot.
- Documentation, runbook-store tagging, and UI flows completed and reviewed.

Next steps (short-term)
-----------------------
1) Kickoff: create a cross-functional task force and schedule weekly 60-minute syncs.
2) Data sprint: label 3,000 high-frequency incidents and publish the labeling SOP by 2026-01-15.
3) Prototype deploy: incident-scorer read-only deploy to us-west-2 by 2026-03-01.

Appendix
-------
- Glossary: "primitive" = smallest executable runbook action (e.g., cache refresh, model swap), "recommendation precision" = fraction of top-1 recommendations that operators judge useful.
- Sample YAML: minimal automation-gateway policy (example)

apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: AutomationPolicy
metadata:
  name: safe-cache-refresh
  region: us-west-2
spec:
  primitives:
    - prefetch_refresh
  approvalsRequired:
    - operator
  maxExecutionsPerHour: 5
  rollbackOnError: true
